Plot Exact Power against the Response Probability of Group 1

Source: R/plot.bbssr_power.R
plot.bbssr_power.Rd

Plot Exact Power against the Response Probability of Group 1

Usage

# S3 method for class 'bbssr_power'
plot(
  x,
  main = NULL,
  sub = NULL,
  xlab = NULL,
  ylab = NULL,
  ylim = c(0, 1),
  show.points = TRUE,
  colours = NULL,
  base_size = 11,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An object of class bbssr_power returned by BinaryPower

main

Title of the plot. The default of NULL builds the title from the object and a single NA drops it

sub

Subtitle of the plot, following the convention of main

xlab

Label of the horizontal axis, following the convention of main

ylab

Label of the vertical axis, following the convention of main

ylim

Numeric vector of length two giving the range of the vertical axis, or NULL for a range chosen from the data

show.points

Logical. If TRUE, the default, a marker is drawn at every evaluated response probability. Set it to FALSE to draw the curve alone, which is easier to read on a fine grid

colours

Colour of the curve

base_size

Base font size of the theme, in points

...

Further arguments, currently ignored

Value

A ggplot object

Details

The vertical range is imposed with coord_cartesian, so points outside ylim are hidden rather than removed from the data.

Examples

pw <- BinaryPower(p1 = seq(0.3, 0.8, by = 0.1), p2 = rep(0.2, 6),
                  N1 = 20, N2 = 20, alpha = 0.025, Test = 'Chisq')
plot(pw)


# Enlarge the type, rescale the vertical axis, rename the axes and drop the markers
plot(pw, base_size = 14, ylim = c(0.2, 1), sub = NA, show.points = FALSE,
     xlab = 'Response probability, experimental group', ylab = 'Exact power')
